$comment: The three store listings this repository ships, in the order each store takes them.
This file is the ONE source for three things a render needs, which is why it is data
rather than a table copied into the HTML: the caption each frame carries, the app
capture that fills its slot, and the harness state that capture was taken from.
`design/preview/capture.mjs --target frames` reads it to render the committed PNGs,
and `design/store-screenshots/capture-frames.mjs` reads it to re-take the app captures
they are made of. Captions are the plan's (`docs/publishing/listing-screenshots.md`,
'The set — nine shots, claim-first order'); changing one is a re-render, not an edit
to a PNG.
`surfaces` is the surface itself: the template that draws it, the canvas the store
requires, the output directory, and the device profile its captures are taken at.
Paths are relative to this directory. `cell` and `scenario` are the mock relay's own
words (`tools/visual/matrix.ts`, `tools/mock-relay/scenarios.ts`): the capture runs
that cell with that world pinned, so the frame is the app rendering a real relay
answer and nothing in it is composited.
`crop` (Play only) is the vertical edge the capture is anchored to inside the slot.
Play's slot is taller than a phone screen, so the template crops the capture rather
than letterboxing it; the per-shot anchors are the plan's ('Mapping onto the
templates'). It is the only field a frame may carry that the other surfaces ignore.
`compareFuzz` (a surface field) is the pixel tolerance, in percent, that
`design/preview/capture.mjs --check` allows when it re-renders a frame and the bytes
differ: how far a pixel's channels may drift before it counts as a difference.
Absent means zero, and zero is what a surface should carry unless a runner has
proved the need: on Chrome 156 the iPad set's nine frames were stale at zero
while all nine iPhone and eight Play frames matched, so only the iPad carries 2.
The check prints the differing-pixel count at zero tolerance beside the tolerated
one, so whether that 2% is still needed can be read off a passing run.
